other_names: The name Verticordia preissii was given to this taxon by Schauer in 1844 and remained valid until the plant was recognized as a variety of V. acerosa by Alex Geraldtom George in 1991. However the name Verticordia preissii has also for many years been incorrectly applied to specimens of both V. endlicheriana Schauer (1846) and V. chrysanthella A.S. George (1991).
Verticordia hirta was a name given to this species by Nicolas Turczaninow in 1852. However the name Verticordia endlicheriana had already been published by Johann Schauer in 1846.

The name Verticordia chrysantha var. preissii was given to a specimen of a form of V. chrysanthella by Schauer in 1844. Specimens of V. chrysanthella have often been incorrectly called V. preissii. The name preissii is correctly applied to a variety of V. acerosa.

In 1847, this species was named and described as Verticordia gilbertii by Russian botanist Nicholas Turczaninow, but the name Verticordia chrysantha had already been published 9 years earlier by Stephan Endlicher.

V. nobilis has for many years been incorrectly known as V. grandiflora, and specimens were mistakenly placed under that taxon until the correct species name, Verticordia nobilis (described by Carl Meisner in 1856), was reinstated by Alex George in 1991.
Chrysorhoe serrata was a name published by John Lindley (1839) but this name was not recognized by other botanists.

The name Chrysorhoe nitens, Lindley (1836), was not accepted by other botanists. Verticordia nitida (Lindley) Endlicher (1839) was described, by the same botanist, one year after the name Verticordia nitens had already been published, apparently an error for nitens.

other_names: Chamelaucium plumosum Desfontaines (1819) and Verticordia fontanesii de Candolle 1828) were the names first given to the specimens collected by Archibald Menzies in October 1791.

Verticordia fontanesii var. brevifolia E. Mueller (1876) is an illegitimate name. Verticordia fontanesii de Candolle var. brachyphylla Diels (1904). Verticordia plumosa var. brevifolia (F. Mueller) Domin (1923).
The name Verticordia pectinata was used by Nicolas Turczaninow in 1852 and Verticordia fontanesii de Candolle var. grandiflora was described by George Bentham in 1867.
Verticordia cespitosa Turczaninow (1847) was a name used for this taxon until it was recognized as a variety of V. densiflora by Alex George.
This taxon was known as Verticordia stelluligera Meisner (1857) until Alex George recognized it as being a variety of V. densiflora. Geraldion®
Chamelaucium brownii Desfontaines (1819) was a name given to this species before Verticordia was described as a separate genus by de Candolle.
For many years V. eriocephala has been incorrectly known V. brownii.

The name Verticordia polytricha was attributed to this species until its distinguishing characteristics were noticed by Bob and Betty Wemm during the 1960s and 1970s whilst assisting with the compilation of a herbarium for the Kalbarri Region. Alex George was made aware of these differences in 1984 and was thus convinced that it should be recognized as a separate species.

The name Verticordia conferta was incorrectly attributed to a specimen of this species by George Bentham in 1867. This species was known as V. minutiflora and V. sp. affinity minutiflora until the name Verticordia vicinella was published by Alex George in 1991.
Verticordia fontanesii var. parviflora was a name used by George Bentham in 1867, 3 years after this species had been described and named V. minutiflora by Ferdinand Mueller.

Verticordia conferta was a name incorrectly attributed to this species by George Bentham in 1867, 15 years after it had already been described and named V. fastigiata by the Russian botanist Turczaninow.
The name Verticordia demissa Ferdinand Mueller ex George Bentham (1867) was incorrectly attributed to this species 15 years after it was described and named by Nicolas Turczaninow.

Chamelaucium verticordinum was described and named in 1864 by Ferdinand Mueller. The name was changed to Darwinia verticordina by George Bentham in 1865. This taxon was then recognized as a Verticordia (with some reservations) by Alex George in his 1991 review of the genus, thus its name was again changed to the present one.
Verticordia sp. affinity penicillaris was the name by which this species was known until it was recognized as a separate entity, described and named V. dasystylis by Alex George in 1991.
This plant was described as Verticordia stylosa by Nicolas Turczaninow in 1847 and this name was used until Alex George recognized the taxon as a variety of V. huegelii.

Verticordia stylotricha was described by Ludwig Diels in 1904, many years after the Russian botanist Nicolas Turczaninow had described and named this species Verticordia brachypoda (in 1847). Confusion has been perpetuated because considerable variation occurs within V. brachypoda and it is possible Geraldtom that some future division into subspecific or varietal status may be warranted. From October 1984, when Mary and Basil Smith collected specimens for the Verticordia Reference Collection, this plant was commonly known as Verticordia affinity roei, until it was described and named by Alex George. Two specimens collected previously by Alice Roach near Dalwallinu in 1981 were in such poor condition they were not recognized until much later.

V. inclusa has often been confused with V. roei and V. insignis. The publication Hooker's Icones Plantarum Series 4, vol. 28, Pl. 2779 (1905) reproduced an illustration by artist Mathilda Smith labelled Verticordia roei. The plant illustrated is named incorrectly and should be labelled V. inclusa.
Verticordia compta was described and named by Stephan Endlicher in 1839. This name remained in use until the plant was recognized as a subspecies of V. insignis by Alex George.
Verticordia umbellata was a name used by the Russian botanist Nicolas Turczaninow in 1847, 3 years after this species had been described and named V. habrantha by Johannes Schauer.
Verticordia callitricha was named and described by Carl Meisner in 1857, thus the name callitricha was retained by Alex George when he recognized this taxon as a variety of V. monadelpha.
Until this species was named and described by Alex George it was commonly known as Verticordia sp. Mt Hampton.
The name Verticordia adenocalyx was given to specimens of this species by Ludwig Diels in 1904, 5 years after V. helmsii had been described and the name published by Spencer Moore.
This species has occasionally been incorrectly labelled and sold in nurseries as 'the eastern form of V. picta?
Verticordia pentandra was described and named by the Russian botanist Nicolas Turczaninow in 1847, 8 years after the name Verticordia picta had been published by Stephan Endlicher.
V. cunninghamii var. longistyla was the name given to this taxon by Charles Gardner in 1923. This name was used until the plant was recognized as a separate species and described by Norman Byrnes.

Verticordia setigera was a name given to this species by English botanist John Lindley, in his Sketch of the Vegetation of the Swan River Colony which was published in 1839. Verticordia drummondii var. lindleyi was a name used by Bentham in 1867.
From the early 1980s until its name was published, this taxon was referred to as Verticordia sp. nov. No. 72.
Before its description in 1991, this species was sometimes referred to as Verticordia spicata.

This taxon was named Verticordia wilhelmii by Ferdinand Mueller in 1855 and was later placed into the genus Homoranthus by mycologist Edwin Cheel, a botanical assistant at the Botanic Gardens in Sydney
